title: Zero-touch Cluster Provisioning Handbook (operatorized) - Draft
content:
Purpose:

This is a working draft for a zero-touch, operatorized on-prem Kubernetes cluster provisioning playbook. The goal is to standardize a reproducible path for bare-metal and vSphere clusters using Cluster API (CAPI) + provider-metal3 (CAPM3) for metal, and CAPI + provider-vsphere for vSphere, with Terraform as the source-of-truth for infrastructure primitives. This doc focuses on the flow, Terraform module design notes, and an upgrade strategy that maps to both machine-managed and control-plane-managed upgrade paths.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform engineers, infra SREs, and solutions engineers who run or deploy Private clusters for customers.
- Scale: single-rack to multi-rack (tens to low hundreds of nodes).
- Environments: airgapped and connected datacenters; vSphere-managed clusters should follow the same logical plan but with provider-specific steps.
- Not covered: deep hardware procurement, datacenter cabling, vendor-specific firmware steps (we link to vendor docs).

Design principles:
- Declarative infra: Terraform defines networks, DNS, BMC credentials vault paths, and image registries.
- Operator-first bootstrap: CAPI treats machines as Kubernetes objects; Metal3 handles PXE/ironic lifecycle without brittle scripts.
- Idempotent runs: re-run TF + CAPI without manual one-off hacks.
- Reversible upgrades: staged rollouts with automated health checks and clear rollback points.

Minimal prerequisites checklist:
- BMC access for each node (IPMI/Redfish credentials stored in vault).
- DHCP scope or dedicated PXE VLAN (managed by Terraform or existing network team).
- TFTP/HTTP image service (can be hosted on an internal registry or a Tinkerbell/Matchbox equivalent).
- Terraform state storage (remote backend, e.g. S3-compatible with locking).
- Kubernetes management cluster reachable from the ops network to run CAPI controllers (this can be a small management cluster or an Operator on an existing management plane).
- Image builder pipeline to publish OS images (CoreOS, Bottlerocket, or Ubuntu cloud images) and container registry mirroring for airgapped installs.

Topology patterns (recommended):
- Small (POC): 3 control-plane nodes, 2 worker nodes, one management node running CAPI controllers hosted off-cluster.
- Production (HA): 5 control-plane nodes across racks, autoscaling worker pools via MachineDeployments, dedicated management cluster with Backup/restore of the management plane.

Terraform modules - organization notes (high level):
- modules/network: VPC/VLAN, subnets, DHCP reservations, PXE VLAN tagging. Inputs: name, cidr, dhcp_ranges (list), pxevlan_id. Outputs: subnet_ids, dhcp_scope_id.
- modules/bmc: BMC credential resources (stores secrets in Vault or KMS), template for per-node BMC secret injection. Inputs: node_list (map), vault_path_prefix. Outputs: bmc_secret_paths.
- modules/image-registry: config for registry mirror (for airgapped), CA bundles, auth credentials. Inputs: registry_host, cert_pem, mirror_enabled. Outputs: registry_push_endpoint.
- modules/capi-bootstrap: lightweight TF to install bootstrap objects (Cluster, KubeadmControlPlane, MachineDeployment) and to upload bare-metal resources for CAPM3. Inputs: cluster_name, k8s_version, control_plane_count, machine_templates. Outputs: cluster_object_id.
- modules/vsphere: resource pool, folder, datacenter references, VM template info for provider-vsphere. Inputs: vcenter_host, datacenter, datastore, template_name. Outputs: vm_template_ids.

Terraform variables conventions (recommendation):
- Use explicit maps for inventory: nodes = { node-01 = { bmc_ip = "10.0.10.5" role = "cp" } }
- Avoid hardcoding credentials; reference vault paths via data lookup resources.
- Tag resources with redwood:team, redwood:env, redwood:cluster for inventory and cost center mapping.

Example terraform snippet (conceptual):
variable "nodes" { type = map(any) }
resource "vault_generic_secret" "bmc" { for_each = var.nodes path = "${var.vault_prefix}/${each.key}/bmc" data_json = jsonencode({ ip = each.value.bmc_ip user = var.bmc_user password = each.value.bmc_pass }) }

Operatorized bootstrap flow (end-to-end):
1) Run Terraform to provision network, storage objects, and BMC secrets. This also registers DHCP reservations and ensures image registry mirroring is ready.
2) Seed the management cluster with CAPI controllers and provider components (CAPM3 or provider-vsphere).
3) Apply Cluster manifest (Cluster, KubeadmControlPlane / MachineDeployment / Metal3MachineTemplate). CAPI creates Machine objects.
4) Metal3 (ironic) handles PXE/inscription -> boot -> provisioning. Watch baremetalhosts progress to "provisioned".
5) CAPI's MachineControllers link the new nodes to the target cluster; node joins and kubelet registers.
6) Post-provision hooks run via DaemonSet to ensure local storage, log collection, and monitoring agents.

Key monitoring events to watch: BareMetalHost registered, BMC power state transitions, image fetch errors, kubelet registration, container runtime readiness, node kubelet conditions.

Airgap considerations:
- Pre-push all images to private mirror and configure imagePullSecrets via the cluster object.
- Embed CA bundles into nodes via ignition/cloud-init or Metal3Provisioning templates.
- Terraform must provision DNS entries for internal registries and adjust cluster imageRepository settings.

Validation smoke tests (automated):
- k get nodes -o wide (expect all nodes Ready)
- curl -f http://internal-registry/healthz
- run a small canary deployment (nginx with 3 replicas) and validate response latency < 200ms across worker nodes.

Upgrade plan (operatorized clusters - recommended safe path):
Philosophy: Prefer control-plane first, then workers; use MachineDeployments and KubeadmControlPlane (or CAPI upgrade controller) to orchestrate rolling updates. Automate health gating and provide manual hold points.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Snapshot management cluster etcd and store in immutable backup (artifact).
- Export current inventory via tfstate and CAPI Cluster object.
- Run e2e smoke tests and capture baseline metrics (token usage, average p50/p99 request latency).
- Ensure cluster autoscaler is disabled for upgrade window.
- Notify customers and open an upgrade ticket with the planned window.

Upgrade phases:
Phase 0 - Canary: select a MachineDeployment labeled 'canary' with 1-2 small nodes. Update its template to target new k8s version/OS image and wait for all canary pods to pass full integration smoke tests (app-level and infra-level).
Phase 1 - Control plane: Use KubeadmControlPlane or CAPI control plane upgrade to incrementally roll control-plane nodes (1 at a time) ensuring etcd quorum and API responsiveness. Validate controllers, CRD health, and that CAPI controllers are stable.
Phase 2 - Workers (MachineDeployments): For each MachineDeployment, increase maxUnavailable to a conservative value (default 1) and roll template updates. Use nodeSelector/toleration-based draining policies to avoid scheduling spikes.
Phase 3 - Post-upgrade validation: run canary traffic, verify Prometheus metrics and tracing, run admission webhook smoke checks, and run any customer-specific regression suites.

Rollback strategy:
- If canary fails, revert MachineDeployment template and redeploy old image (TF or kubectl apply) and mark cluster as paused.
- If control plane upgrade causes quorum loss, restore management cluster snapshot or revert KubeadmControlPlane rollout to previous revision via CAPI (control-plane objects hold revision history).
- Maintain immutable image tags so rollback can fetch exact pre-upgrade artifacts.

Troubleshooting notes (common failure modes):
- BMC credentials wrong: check vault path, try ipmitool/redfishctl against BMC, verify network ACLs.
- PXE network misconfigured: confirm DHCP options 66/67, TFTP/HTTP endpoints, and VLAN tagging reachable from the node's NIC.
- Image fetch failures in airgapped env: confirm registry mirror credentials and CA; test with curl/wget from an ops jump host.
- Kubelet deadloop: check container runtime logs (crictl), disk pressure, and cloud-init/ignition user-data exit codes.

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Watch metal3 BareMetalHost status: kubectl -n metal3 get baremetalhosts -o wide
- Inspect CAPI Machine status: kubectl get machines -A -o wide --selector=cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name=<cluster>
- Force requeue BMH: kubectl annotate bmh <name> metal3.io/force-change=true --overwrite

Template for upgrade run card (to be used in Incident/Change system):
- Change ID: (autogenerated)
- Cluster: <cluster>
- Window: <start/end time>
- Responsible engineers: <owner, oncall, approver>
- Rollout steps: Canary -> Control plane -> Workers -> Validation
- Abort criteria: API errors >5% for 5m, >10% pod restarts within 10m in system namespaces, etcd member count mismatch.
- Rollback steps: documented above.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Integrate pre-provision VNF tests (switch port checks) into Terraform apply pipeline?
- Standardize a single image builder pipeline for Bottlerocket + Ubuntu variants used across customers.
- Add terraform plan gating and automatic plan approvals for repeatable fleets.

Appendix: quick TF variable example (compact)
variable "cluster_name" { default = "redwood-onprem-prod" }
variable "nodes" { default = { "rack1-cp-01" = { bmc_ip = "10.2.10.21" role = "controlplane" }, "rack1-wk-01" = { bmc_ip = "10.2.10.31" role = "worker" } } }

# module usage sketch
module "network" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//network" name = var.cluster_name cidr = "10.2.0.0/16" }
module "bmc" { source = "../modules/bmc" nodes = var.nodes vault_prefix = "secret/private-deployments/${var.cluster_name}" }

-- end of draft --

Notes: This doc intentionally leans operator-first; it assumes our future-state goal is to reduce one-off imperative scripts and to increase observability during every phase of bootstrap and upgrade. Feedback welcome; next steps are to translate the above into a scannable runbook play with exact command references and to add a vSphere-specific appendix with VM template lifecycle steps.
